title: Detached VPC Snapshot Handshake - PRD (rough)
content:
Summary

Problem: customers running Redwood Private in network environments with intermittent connectivity (air-gapped maintenance windows, flaky peering, scheduled egress windows) need a resilient way to deliver approval events and audit log snapshots to Redwood control plane without compromising audit integrity or delaying approval gating for critical route changes. Existing designs assume continuous connectivity and synchronous handshakes — that model breaks in highly constrained customer-managed networks.

Proposal: define a "detached snapshot handshake" protocol and PRD that supports: incremental, tamper-evident audit snapshots; offline-first temporary escrow; idempotent replays and resumable handshakes; a dual-mode approval flow that allows local emergency approvals while preserving cryptographic proof-of-consent for later reconciliation.

Goals
- Ensure audit integrity: every local approval or operator action has a verifiable cryptographic capsule that can be later ingested by Redwood and validated end-to-end.
- Support intermittent networks: allow customers to stage snapshots locally and push or authorize push when connectivity available.
- Keep platform trust: no silent bypass of approval gates — all emergency/local fallbacks must create audit evidence and an elevated review path by default.
- Minimize operational burden: simple UX for operators, deterministic conflict resolution rules, and clear backfill semantics.

Out of scope (for initial delivery)
- Full HSM integration for customer-managed keys (we will use customer-provided PEMs or Redwood-managed keys depending on tier).
- Deep analytics UI in the Console; we will provide a compact ingest format and a Console integration in a follow-on.

User personas
- Customer network operator (primary): needs to make urgent firewall/VPC changes during maintenance windows, often with temporary disconnection from Redwood.
- Platform engineer at customer: responsible for compliance and audit exports; will consume proofs for internal postmortem.
- Redwood SRE/Product: needs to ingest snapshots, validate signatures, surface conflicts, and trigger follow-up approval or rollback flows.

Key concepts and terminology
- Snapshot capsule: a compact, compressed archive (gzipped jsonl) containing a window of sequential audit events and metadata.
- Envelope header: metadata for a capsule including sequence_start, sequence_end, capsule_id (UUID), signer_pubkey_fingerprint, timestamp, and proof_of_integrity (SHA256 digest).
- Local-Approval token (LAT): a time-limited token created by an operator when connectivity absent. LAT includes operator identity, reason, risk-tag, TTL, and is signed locally. LAT is always accompanied by a snapshot capsule on next sync or immediate push if available.
- Reconciliation receipt: Redwood-produced signed assertion after successful ingestion and validation of a capsule; includes canonical sequence range and ingest_id.

High-level flow (detached mode)
1. Operator initiates change via local Console/CLI. System validates policy; if an approval gate would normally call Redwood, the local agent creates a LAT and writes an audit event + capsule entry with event_seq = N. The action proceeds locally (if policy allows emergency fallback).
2. The agent persists the capsule to local storage and marks it PENDING_PUSH. If connectivity present, it attempts push. If disconnected, the capsule persists until connectivity restored.
3. On push, the agent opens a TLS connection to Redwood Ingest API, performs a capability handshake (mutual TLS or token + proof), and uploads the envelope header + capsule. The agent also provides a capsule signature using the configured key.
4. Redwood validates signature, integrity digest, and sequence continuity against previous ingest receipts. If gaps or overlaps, Redwood responds with detailed reconciliation instructions (accept, conflict-report, request full replay).
5. On success, Redwood emits a reconciliation receipt signed back to customer and marks the associated LAT as recorded in system for future audit lookup.

Message formats (examples)
- Envelope header (JSON line): {"capsule_id":"uuid-...", "sequence_start":"12345", "sequence_end":"12362", "signer_fingerprint":"sha256:ab12...", "digest":"sha256:ef34...", "timestamp":"2025-01-10T14:12:00Z"}  (gzipped capsule body follows)
- LAT example (base64-signed blob): operator:diego@example.com; action:apply-vpc-route; reason:"rolling upgrade"; ts:2025-01-10T14:10Z; ttl:48h; sig:base64(...)

Acceptance criteria
- Agent can generate and persist capsules while offline without data loss in 99.99% of simulated disconnect cycles (test harness-based).
- Redwood ingest API can validate capsule digest and signer and return reconciliation receipt within SLO for 99% of small capsules (<1MB).
- In conflict scenarios (overlapping seq ranges), Redwood returns a deterministic conflict resolution response with one of: merge-accepted, request-full-replay, or mark-for-manual-review.
- LATs are stored and linked to the final ingest receipt; console displays where LAT was used and provides download of original signed blob.

Approval gates behavior and policies
- Normal mode: approvals require wired handshake with Redwood.
- Detached mode (network failure or scheduled maintenance): operator may invoke an emergency approval with LAT. LATs are limited by policy: configurable per-customer TTL, max outstanding LATs, and allowed actions. All LAT usage must be flagged for high-priority post-ingest review.
- Automatic escalation: if LAT use exceeds threshold (e.g., 5 LATs in 24h), Redwood flags the account and may require a human review before subsequent LATs are allowed.

Audit integrity and tamper-evidence
- Capsules are chained by previous_digest in the envelope header to provide tamper-evidence across multiple capsules. Redwood verifies chain and sequence continuity on ingest; any break marks the chain as suspect and triggers forensic mode.
- Signatures: support both customer-supplied RSA/ECDSA keys and Redwood-managed signing on behalf (enterprise tier). Fingerprints recorded in envelope header.
- Immutable storage: once ingested, Redwood writes ingest metadata to an append-only ledger (immutable store) and emits reconciliation receipts.

Edge cases and failure modes
- Partial uploads: agent should support resumable chunked upload for capsules >5MB. Server must validate partial digests incrementally.
- Clock skew: LATs include operator timestamp and server validates within acceptable skew window (configurable up to 5m default). For larger skew, agent must include previously-signed NTP-anchor events.
- Lost capsules: if agent storage was accidentally pruned, customer can rehydrate from operator-run exports but Redwood will mark the sequence gap and require manual reconciliation.

Operational rollout plan (MVP timeline 10 weeks)
- Week 0-2: prototype agent changes (persist capsules, create LAT) + define envelope schema.
- Week 3-5: implement ingest API endpoints + basic validation and ledger write.
- Week 6: build CLI/console flags for detached mode toggle and LAT creation UX.
- Week 7-8: internal e2e tests with simulated connectivity interruptions and conflict injection.
- Week 9: invite 2 pilot customers (one financial with strict retention, one infra-heavy startup) for beta.
- Week 10: collect feedback, tighten security posture, prepare production release notes.

Metrics and success criteria
- Time-to-receipt: median time from push to reconciliation receipt < 500ms for small capsules.
- LAT incidence: % of total approvals using LAT should be trackable; success target < 2% for customers not in maintenance windows.
- Conflict rate: target conflict responses < 0.5% of ingests.

Compliance mapping
- SOC2/ISO: capsules include operator identity and RTC time; ledger retention configurable for legal holds.
- GDPR: ability to export capsule contents for DSAR; ingested blobs indexed by customer id and subject to export requests.

Open questions / decisions required
- Key management: accept customer HSM-stored keys for signing or delay to later phase? (security team input needed)
- TTL and policy defaults for LATs across enterprise tiers.
- UI: how to surface chains and conflicts in Console without overwhelming customers? (product/UX input)

Next steps
- Security review for envelope schema and signature validation (assign to Sana).
- Prototype agent changes and send to infra team for feedback (assign to Benji).
- Draft ingest API contract and add to PRIV-4023 (assign to Diego).

Notes to self / rough TODOs
- Mock up reconciliation-receipt sample JSON.
- Create small test corpus generator for capsule chaining.
- Add instrumentation points for LAT frequency and operator identity exposures.

Appendix: quick sample sequence (operator perspective)
1) ashaiyer@cust: ./redwood-agent apply-route --cidr 10.2.0.0/24 --egress gw-1 --detached
2) agent: validate policy -> create LAT(B64) -> write event seq 1012 to capsule C-2025-01-10-14-12 -> respond OK locally
3) later when network available: agent pushes C-2025-01-10-14-12 -> Redwood validates -> issues receipt R-9983 -> Console shows "detached capsule ingested, LAT linked"

End of draft.

-- Asha
